uk-cpi-2026-10.standing: The Office for National Statistics' monthly consumer price index, the measure the Bank of England targets at 2%. It shapes the path of interest rates and feeds into wage settlements, benefits and pensions across the UK.
uk-cpi-2026-10.recent: The Office for National Statistics reports UK consumer price inflation for September, settling where the headline rate stood as the month closed.

fomc-2026-10.standing: The Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee meets eight times a year to set the federal funds rate. Its decisions pass through to US borrowing costs, the dollar and credit conditions worldwide.
fomc-2026-10.recent: Last month the Fed raised rates 12-0, tightening into a supply shock caused by a closed strait and defying Trump's calls to lower them. This meeting settles whether that hike was a single answer to war-driven inflation or the first of several, with the president pressing the other way.

ecb-2026-10.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets about every six weeks to set interest rates for the countries that share the euro. Its deposit rate reaches mortgages, company loans and government borrowing across the bloc.
ecb-2026-10.recent: The European Central Bank meets after the Fed voted 12-0 to raise rates over a closed strait, and after the Bank of Japan went to 1.25%, a 31-year high. Frankfurt has to decide whether the same supply shock is a reason to tighten or one to look through.

boj-2026-10.standing: The Bank of Japan's nine-member Policy Board, which meets eight times a year to set the short-term policy rate. Its decisions move the yen, Japanese government bond yields and the global trades funded by borrowing cheaply in yen.
boj-2026-10.recent: The board meets for the first time since last month's hike to a 31-year high, made to curb rising prices, after which the BOJ governor's 75-minute briefing failed to win over markets. This meeting shows whether that case holds, and how any further tightening fits a balancing act with Bessent that is already getting harder.

boe-2026-11.standing: The Bank of England's nine-member Monetary Policy Committee, which meets eight times a year to set Bank Rate. Its votes pass through to British mortgage and savings rates within weeks, and sterling moves with them.
boe-2026-11.recent: The Bank of England sets its policy rate at this meeting, and with it the cost of the mortgages and savings that track it. The committee votes member by member, so the decision also shows how its members divide on the path ahead.

fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee, which meets eight times a year to set the federal funds rate. Its decisions set the price of dollar credit worldwide, from US mortgages to emerging-market debt.
fomc-2026-12.recent: The Fed last moved with a 12-0 hike, tightening into a supply shock caused by a closed strait, against Trump's calls to lower rates. This meeting settles whether that was a single step against war-driven inflation or the first of several, and whether a committee that voted as one still does under that political pressure.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The Group of Twenty: 19 major economies plus the EU and the African Union, whose leaders meet once a year under a rotating presidency. Its agreements set the agenda on debt relief, trade and financial rules for most of the world's output.
g20-2026-miami.recent: Rubio has invited Vladimir Putin, who is wanted by the ICC, to the Miami summit in December, and the Kremlin is considering it. The US is outside the court's jurisdiction, so the invitation tests whether the other leaders will sit at a table with a man the court wants arrested.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council sets interest rates for every country that uses the euro, meeting about every six weeks. Its decisions reach mortgages, business loans and government borrowing across the bloc, and the euro moves with them.
ecb-2026-12.recent: The European Central Bank's rate decision sets what banks pay to borrow from it and what they earn on money parked with it for the months after. Nothing reported so far makes this meeting different from a routine one.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee meets eight times a year to set Bank Rate. Its decisions flow into British mortgage costs, business borrowing and savings rates, and sterling and gilt yields move with them.
boe-2026-12.recent: This meeting sets the Bank of England's policy rate and, through it, what British households and firms pay to borrow and earn on savings in the months after.

boj-2026-12.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which meets eight times a year to set Japan's short-term policy rate. After decades near zero, its moves reach Japanese mortgages and deposits, and carry through the yen into global funding markets.
boj-2026-12.recent: The Bank of Japan's last move was a hike to curb rising prices, and its balancing act with Bessent was already described as only going to get harder. This meeting settles whether that hike stands alone or opens a run of them, with borrowers in Japan on one side of the answer and savers on the other.

fred-us-gdp-2026-09-30.standing: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's quarterly measure of everything the US economy produces, published in successive estimates as fuller data arrives. It sets the baseline that the Fed, bond markets and budget forecasters work from.
fred-us-gdp-2026-09-30.recent: The OECD has just forecast that the U.S. economy will outgrow its allies, crediting an AI boom it expects to offset the Middle East energy shock for now. This release is the hard-data test of that argument: whether AI investment is showing up in measured output strongly enough to carry the economy through dearer energy.

fred-us-pce-2026-09-30.standing: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's monthly report on US personal income and spending. It carries the PCE price index, the inflation gauge the Federal Reserve targets, so it moves rate expectations, Treasury yields and the dollar.
fred-us-pce-2026-09-30.recent: The Bureau of Economic Analysis publishes the latest US PCE figures, which settle how fast consumer prices and household spending ran over the month. That is the inflation reading the next rate decision is weighed against.

fred-us-jobs-report-2026-10-02.standing: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly employment report: a payroll count from a survey of employers and an unemployment rate from a survey of households. Bond yields, the dollar and interest-rate expectations all reset on it.
fred-us-jobs-report-2026-10-02.recent: The US jobs report publishes the latest payroll count and unemployment rate. It settles whether hiring kept pace over the past month, and it gives rate-setters and markets a fresh read on the labour market.
